# What am I doing today?

Always Today is a calm to-do list that answers that one question every morning. Your lists live on your device, work offline and open at once, and they sync across your phone, your computer and your terminal when you want them to.

See how it works Free on one device

Out now on Google Play for Android phones and Googlebooks, on the App Store for iPhone and iPad, in the Microsoft Store for Windows, and as a download for the Mac , the Linux terminal and Linux desktops .

## Quiet, quick, and yours

Today, Upcoming, Anytime, Someday and a Logbook; areas and projects with headings; repeats that never double up; reminders. And four things that make it different.

- Your lists live on your device Everything works offline and opens at once, because each device keeps its own full copy. On one device you don't need an account at all. Sign in with just your email to sync. A change reaches your other devices when they next open, or within a few minutes while they're open, and two devices editing different parts of the same to-do both keep their changes.

## One list on every screen you have

The same lists and the same keys everywhere, so what your hands learn on one device works on the next.

### Android phone

A home-screen widget, reminders, and sharing from any app. Say a few to-dos one after another and the phone writes them down, understood on the phone itself.

Get it on Google Play

### Googlebook

On a Googlebook it behaves like a desktop app: two panes, keyboard shortcuts, right-click menus and a window you can resize.

### Windows PC

A shortcut that works anywhere, Ctrl Alt Space , opens quick entry, and the tray icon keeps it a click away.

Get it from the Microsoft Store

### Mac

Close the window and it waits in the menu bar, with quick entry a click away. For Macs with Apple silicon.

### Linux terminal, made on Omarchy

A fast native app that starts at once and takes your terminal's colours. Keys feel like Vim. The same program adds to-dos from scripts, puts Today in your bar and opens a one-line capture prompt.

Prefer a window? The window app is the same app as on the Mac. It shares the terminal app's lists and follows your desktop's light or dark.

Download for the terminal

Download the window app

On Arch or Omarchy, one line installs each as a package. The terminal app:

curl -L -o always-today.pkg.tar.zst https://alwaystoday.uk/download/linux-terminal && sudo pacman -U always-today.pkg.tar.zst

The window app:

curl -L -o always-today-desktop.pkg.tar.zst https://alwaystoday.uk/download/linux-desktop && sudo pacman -U always-today-desktop.pkg.tar.zst

For iPhone and iPad, download it on the App Store .

## Free on one device, for ever

Every feature, with no account. You pay only to sync between devices, and one plan covers every device you sign in on.

UK prices, VAT included. Every new account gets 7 days of sync free, with no card needed, and refunds come within 14 days with no questions asked. On Android you buy through Google Play; on iPhone and iPad through the App Store, at Apple's own prices of Â£23.99 a year, Â£2.99 a month and Â£58.99 for Lifetime; on Windows, Mac and Linux through Stripe's secure checkout in your browser. The Assistant is its own subscription: on the web you choose the amount; in the App Store and Google Play it's Â£2.49, Â£4.99 or Â£9.99 a month, and every amount gets the same Assistant.

Yes, on one device, for ever: every list, quick entry, repeats, reminders, import and export. You pay only if you want your lists to sync between devices: Â£24 a year, Â£3 a month, or Â£59 once for Lifetime. Every new account gets 7 days of sync free, with no card needed.

From inside the app. On Windows, Mac and Linux it opens Stripe's secure checkout in your browser; Stripe sells the plan through its Managed Payments service, shown on your receipt as Onelink. Yes: refunds within 14 days, no questions asked, on top of your legal rights. The help page explains how, for the web, Google Play and the App Store.

Rows that are really questions, such as finding a plumber, comparing two air fryers or checking opening hours, carry a small mark. Press it and an AI does the legwork with web search, then writes the answer back into the row with its sources. Accept it and the to-do is done, or send it back with a note. It sees only the to-do you hand it, never the rest of your lists. You can also connect your own Claude or ChatGPT instead, at no extra cost.

No. Without one, everything stays on your device. An account, just your email address with no password, is only needed to sync.

Not if you turn on end-to-end encryption: your devices encrypt every change before it leaves, with a passphrase only you know. Without it, your lists are stored on the server as written, protected in transit and at rest, and never read, sold or analysed. A to-do you hand to the Assistant is the one exception: the server opens that one to-do and sends it to Anthropic, which runs the AI, as the privacy policy explains.

Yes. Always Today imports their exports and shows you what it found before adding anything. You can export everything as a JSON file at any time.
